sentences.text:
Coram :Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Gautam Kumar Choudhary .........
For the Petitioners : Mr. Vijayant Verma, Advocate For the State : Mr. V. S. Sahay, App ......
05/ 18.08.2023.

Apprehending their arrest, petitioners above-named have moved this Court for
grant of anticipatory bail in connection with Ormanjhi P.S. Case No.163 of 2021 registered under
Sections 406, 420, 467, 468, 471, 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that the alleged offence under Sections 406 &
420 IPC will not be made out as against them as the Sale deed was executed by the petitioner(s) on the strength of power of attorney executed by accused no.1 to 6 who happens to be the joint family members of the informant/complainant.
There was no intention to deceive as under the bona-fide belief the sale-deed(s) was executed.
The main grievance of the complainant/ informant is that without proper partition the share has been disposed of by accused no.1 to 6.
The dispute between the parties is civil in nature.
Learned APP for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer.
Considering the submissions of learned counsel and the fact as discussed above, the anticipatory bail application is allowed.

Hence,
in the event of their arrest or surrender within a period of three weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order before the learned court below, the petitioners named above shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Court below, subject to the conditions laid down under Section 438(2) Cr. P.C.

The petitioners will co-operate in the investigation and will appear on notice under Section 41 A of Cr.P.C. as and when their presence is required and comply with the condition as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C.
(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) Sandeep/uploaded.
